2. Resources, connections and symbols

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-02-connect.Rmd
book-02-connect.Rmd

What you will learn

Attach a resource and learn the two kinds of name used in a session.

This chapter uses the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection from Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

One connection list

A connection is a logged-in session. Our DSLite helper made one, named site.

names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

Most calls accept conns. Passing it explicitly makes clear where a request goes.

The Opal login path

Requires a real Opal. This is the single connection configuration to change when moving to another practice host. Use it instead of the DSLite login from chapter 0. Set the three BOOK_OPAL_* environment variables in your secure local configuration; the URL comes from your administrator or easy-opal setup. This deployment block is not part of the recorded DSLite execution.

opal_url <- Sys.getenv("BOOK_OPAL_URL")
opal_project <- "practice"
opal_resources <- c(gibleed = "gibleed", numeric = "numeric")
lesson_resource <- "gibleed"  # choose "numeric" for numeric chapters
library(DSOpal)
builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()
builder$append(server = "site", url = opal_url,
               user = Sys.getenv("BOOK_OPAL_USER"),
               password = Sys.getenv("BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD"), driver = "OpalDriver")
conns <- DSI::datashield.login(builder$build(), assign = FALSE)
ds.omop.connect(resource = paste(opal_project, opal_resources[[lesson_resource]],
                                 sep = "."), conns = conns)

Reuse this login for every practice lesson, choosing its named resource. The questionnaire-fixture chapters explicitly use their separate local helper. Credentials belong in secure configuration, never a shared notebook. The executed DSLite login is in tools/book/practice.R.

A resource is a route to a database

A resource stores the connection details on the server. On the practice server its name is gibleed. In the optional Opal setup it is practice.gibleed.

A symbol is an R object name inside the DataSHIELD session. Attach the resource and deliberately name the session handle omop:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "gibleed", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)

The server opens its database connection. This does not copy the database into R on your laptop. On Opal, replace only gibleed with the resource name you were given.

Reuse the handle 

ds.omop.columns("person", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$site
#>                    column_name cdm_datatype db_datatype      concept_role

Subsequent calls can omit symbol because its default is omop. An output symbol such as D_people is different: it names a table built later by a recipe.

End a session deliberately

At the end of your own work, call ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns) and then DSI::datashield.logout(conns). Start again with the practice helper for another chapter. The reproduction script performs both cleanup calls after each chapter.

Switch between the two practice resources

The same practice server also offers the numeric Synthea27Nj database. Disconnect the current OMOP handle, then attach that resource on the same login connection:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
numeric_session <- ds.omop.connect(resource = "numeric", conns = conns)
class(numeric_session)
#> [1] "omop_session"

This changes the database behind the OMOP handle. It does not copy or combine patient rows between resources. On Opal the corresponding name is practice.numeric. Return to GiBleed for the next introductory chapters:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
session <- ds.omop.connect(resource = "gibleed", conns = conns)
class(session)
#> [1] "omop_session"

The numeric chapters will open their own fresh numeric session. Keeping resource selection explicit prevents accidentally running a lab recipe against GiBleed’s empty numeric-value fields.

Recap

The resource identifies a database; omop is its session handle; D_people will name a private result.

Try it

Repeat the column request without specifying the symbol.
